messages:
maya: Quick question — I just landed a Terraform change that swaps our SA creation from `kubernetes_service_account` -> using `eks_irsa` module which annotates with `eks.amazonaws.com/role-arn`. Pods now fail with `NoCredentialProviders` in the app logs. Anyone seen this with projected SA tokens?

liam: hmm, did the cluster OIDC provider get created/linked for that account? IRSA requires the cluster OIDC provider ARN present in AWS and the trust policy for the role.

maya: I'm pretty sure the module created the OIDC provider (we call the module from infra-account). The role shows up and annotation is present on the SA: `eks.amazonaws.com/role-arn: arn:aws:iam::111111111111:role/rdw-infra-eks-irsa-app`.

sophie: Could be the pod spec — are you using projected serviceAccount tokens or relying on the old mounted token? EKS >=1.22 defaults to projected token for service account tokens created with TokenRequest API. If `automountServiceAccountToken: false` the pod won't get it.

maya: Pod spec has no `automountServiceAccountToken` set. I verified `kubectl -n infra get sa app-sa -o yaml` and it shows the annotation.

liam: run `kubectl -n infra get pod <pod> -o yaml | grep -A5 projected` — check for `projected` volume under the pod. Also `kubectl -n infra exec -it <pod> -- cat /var/run/secrets/eks.amazonaws.com/serviceaccount/token` to confirm token exists (if allowed).

maya: ran checks — here's the SA yaml excerpt:```yaml
apiVersion: v1
kind: ServiceAccount
metadata:
  name: app-sa
  namespace: infra
  annotations:
    eks.amazonaws.com/role-arn: arn:aws:iam::111111111111:role/rdw-infra-eks-irsa-app
```
No `automountServiceAccountToken` present. Pod's volumes: I see `projected` volume and token file exists at `/var/run/secrets/eks.amazonaws.com/serviceaccount/token`. But app still logs AWS SDK error `NoCredentialProviders: no valid providers in chain` when calling S3.

sophie: Two quick things: 1) Is the IAM role trust policy allowing `sts:AssumeRoleWithWebIdentity` for the exact OIDC provider `sub` condition? Usually the trust uses `sts:AssumeRoleWithWebIdentity` with `Condition: StringEquals: {"oidc.eks.<region>.amazonaws.com/id/<id>:sub": "system:serviceaccount:infra:app-sa"}` or a wildcard like `system:serviceaccount:infra:*`. 2) Are the IAM permissions (policy) attached to the role sufficient for S3?

maya: Trust policy currently uses `StringEquals` on `sub` = `system:serviceaccount:infra:app-sa`. The role has S3 read policy.

liam: If the token exists and trust/policy look good, the other culprit is that the app process might be reading credentials from env vars or default credential chain that prefers ECS/EC2 metadata over IMDS v2 or the projected token provider. What language/runtime?

maya: Node 18 app using AWS SDK v3. We don't set AWS_* env variables. The container base image includes aws-cli for occasional debugging.

sophie: Node SDK v3 should pick up web identity if `AWS_SDK_LOAD_CONFIG` or `AWS_WEB_IDENTITY_TOKEN_FILE`? Actually the SDK looks for `AWS_ROLE_ARN`/`AWS_WEB_IDENTITY_TOKEN_FILE` only when using explicit env var flow. For IRSA, the SDK uses the default credential provider which checks the `WebIdentityTokenFile` provider when environment variables `AWS_WEB_IDENTITY_TOKEN_FILE` and `AWS_ROLE_ARN` are set — but the recommended flow on EKS is that the kubelet syncs projected token and the SDK's web identity provider is used by frameworks that read token file and role ARN env variables. However recent SDKs support the `STS AssumeRoleWithWebIdentity` flow automatically if env vars present.

liam: Wait — in many EKS/IRSA setups the kubelet does NOT set `AWS_ROLE_ARN` or `AWS_WEB_IDENTITY_TOKEN_FILE` env vars into the pod. Instead, the SDK (on some platforms) has built-in support for IRSA by looking at the projected token path by default? This is runtime-dependent. To be certain, we can inject env vars via the deployment spec:```yaml
env:
  - name: AWS_ROLE_ARN
    valueFrom:
      fieldRef:
        fieldPath: metadata.annotations['eks.amazonaws.com/role-arn']
  - name: AWS_WEB_IDENTITY_TOKEN_FILE
    value: '/var/run/secrets/eks.amazonaws.com/serviceaccount/token'
```But k8s doesn't allow reading annotations into env var like that (metadata.annotations not supported in fieldRef) — so that's not viable.

sophie: Right — we usually don't set AWS_ROLE_ARN env var. The common approach: SDK versions that support `webIdentityTokenFile` default path will automatically look at `/var/run/secrets/eks.amazonaws.com/serviceaccount/token` if `AWS_WEB_IDENTITY_TOKEN_FILE` is set or if library supports default. For Node, using `@aws-sdk/credential-providers` there's `fromTokenFile` and other helpers. In many apps you need to enable the WebIdentity provider explicitly or rely on the runtime to wire it.

maya: Interesting — we pinned SDK a while back. Could be outdated. What's the quickest check?

liam: Exec into the pod and run a tiny Node snippet to see which provider chain picks credentials, or run `env` to ensure no AWS env vars interfering. Also `kubectl -n infra exec -it <pod> -- ls -l /var/run/secrets/eks.amazonaws.com/serviceaccount/` to see token and ca.crt.

maya: did that — token + ca.crt present. No AWS_* env vars. I ran `node -e "const {defaultProvider} = require('@aws-sdk/credential-provider-node'); defaultProvider()().then(console.log).catch(console.error)"` and it errors same `NoCredentialProviders`.

sophie: That suggests SDK isn't checking web identity by default. Quick workaround: upgrade SDK or change code to use `fromNodeProviderChain`/`fromWebToken` with `AWS_ROLE_ARN` and token file path. Alternatively use kube2iam/kube2aws? But we prefer IRSA.

maya: For short term I can patch the deployment to set env var `AWS_ROLE_ARN` to the same role ARN (hardcoding) and `AWS_WEB_IDENTITY_TOKEN_FILE=/var/run/secrets/eks.amazonaws.com/serviceaccount/token` to confirm it fixes things. If that works, we know code path is the issue.

liam: yeah do that in a canary. If it works, follow up with either SDK upgrade or explicit credential provider usage in app. Also document it in infra README.

maya: will try now and report back. Thanks! :thumbsup:

devops-bot: Deployment rdw-infra/app-v2 updated (rollout started) — canary pods running.

maya: Canary passed — app started calling S3 successfully after env var injection. Will open PR to bump `@aws-sdk` and add a fallback provider. Also adding a note in infra/irsa.md about verifying SDK support for web identity before switching SA wiring.

sophie: Nice. One more note for Terraform: when you migrated SA creation, ensure you didn't change `automountServiceAccountToken` to `false` in any rollout config. That can break projected tokens.

maya: good call — will double-check. Thanks everyone.
